questiontext.text:
Goal

A web company replaces its builder class with functional options and direct construction. Make both ways of creating a server display the same settings.

Read
  • net/http.Server. Read the field comments for Addr and ReadTimeout. Which address replaces an empty Addr? Which timeout values mean no limit? In the function index, which Java-style API is absent?
Coming from Java

The reflex is a builder class with one setter per field and a build method that fills in the defaults. Go has no overloading, so you cannot write the telescoping constructors that usually precede a builder either. Watch for the habit of resolving the defaults inside the constructor.

Server s = new ServerBuilder()
    .addr(":8080")
    .readTimeout(30)
    .build();
Stuck? Two nudges inside
  • The second sentence of the field comment above Addr covers the empty case.
  • The ReadTimeout field comment covers more than one kind of value in a single sentence. Find that sentence before you write the condition.

Goal

A ferry manifest lists accepted bookings and counts those rejected for too few seats. Read through interchangeable sources, stopping when a booking cannot be identified.

Read
  • io.EOF. Read the complete comment, including the bracketed text. What does it forbid? What reason does it give?
  • io.Reader. Find its declaration under Types. How many methods does it contain? How many methods does the Writer declaration contain?
Coming from Java

The reflex is a BookingRepository interface declared beside its BookingRepositoryImpl, carrying every method the store can offer. The second reflex is one checked exception per failure, caught by exception type at the top of the chain.

public interface BookingRepository { ... }
public class BookingRepositoryImpl implements BookingRepository { ... }

try {
    manifest(repo);
} catch (TooFewSeatsException e) {
    rejected++;
}
Stuck? Two nudges inside
  • The Variables section of the io page declares six errors. Read every line of the comment above each one before you choose.
  • Read how errors.Is recognises a cause after another caller adds context.

testcode.text: l := NewLedger("kea", []Booking{{Ref: "kea-1", Seats: 2}, {Ref: "kea-3", Seats: 4}}) m, err := Manifest(l) fmt.Println(m) fmt.Println(err == nil)

expected.text: kea-1 x2; kea-3 x4; rejected 0 true

testcode.text: l := NewLedger("kea", []Booking{{Ref: "kea-1", Seats: 2}, {Ref: "kea-2", Seats: 0}, {Ref: "kea-3", Seats: 4}}) m, err := Manifest(l) fmt.Println(m) fmt.Println(err == nil)

expected.text: kea-1 x2; kea-3 x4; rejected 1 true

testcode.text: l := NewLedger("kea", nil) _, err := l.Next() fmt.Println(err) rm, rErr := Manifest(Repeat(Booking{Ref: "kea-9", Seats: 2}, 3)) fmt.Println(rm) fmt.Println(rErr == nil)

expected.text: EOF kea-9 x2; kea-9 x2; kea-9 x2; rejected 0 true

testcode.text: l := NewLedger("kea", []Booking{{Ref: "kea-1", Seats: 2}, {Ref: "kea-3", Seats: 4}}, WithMinSeats(3)) m, err := Manifest(l) fmt.Println(m) fmt.Println(err == nil) bad := NewLedger("tui", []Booking{{Ref: "tui-1", Seats: 1}, {Seats: 2}}) _, badErr := Manifest(bad) fmt.Println(badErr)

expected.text: kea-3 x4; rejected 1 true manifest: ledger tui: entry 2: no reference

testcode.text: l := NewLedger("tui", []Booking{{Seats: 0}, {Ref: "tui-1", Seats: 0}, {Ref: "tui-2", Seats: 1}}) _, err := l.Next() fmt.Println(err) _, err = l.Next() fmt.Println(err) b, err := l.Next() fmt.Println(b, err == nil) m, err := Manifest(Repeat(Booking{Ref: "unused", Seats: 1}, 0)) fmt.Println(m, err == nil)

expected.text: ledger tui: entry 1: no reference ledger tui: booking tui-1: too few seats {tui-2 1} true rejected 0 true
